items.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And it turned me on. So I started playing like Bud

ctx.x: I remember you saying when you first heard bop that you were with a group of people who, obviously somebody had introduced it to you who said this is great stuff, and the other people or person you were with said no, no, no, don’t play that.

Yeah the man I was playing with: “You don’t want to play that garbage.” And the first time, I was very young then, I was maybe 17 or 18, somewhere in there, and I heard a young alto player who was playing like Charlie Parker, and I had never heard Charlie Parker before I heard this alto player. He was about my age. And wow, it just touched me, and he had his buddy, who was playing trumpet like Dizzy. In fact in Chicago they used to call this guy “Little Diz.” And it turned me on. So I started playing like Bud

Powell, because I started listening to records, and I was working with this group which was primarily a rhythm and blues group, that’s what you would call it today. And strange enough, the saxophone player and the drummer in the group were also turned on by bebop. So the drummer just got tired of brow beating. You know, “Man why don’t you play straight, what are you dropping all those bombs for?” And he quit. And after a while the saxophone player quit.
